title: Reduce prefill-side tokenizer overhead via fast-path tokenization & caching
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Tokenization and prompt preprocessing in the prefill stage are a measurable CPU-bound overhead for short-to-medium prompts. Profiling across hosted nodes shows a 8-18ms median per-request overhead from tokenizer + normalization + proto conversions for typical N=1 requests, and a disproportionate p95 tail. This increases cost and adds brittle tail latency for low-token requests (chat messages, completion prompts).

Goal: Reduce prefill-side overhead by introducing a tokenization fast-path and a multi-layer pretokenized cache. Target: p50 tokenization latency <4ms and p95 <10ms for common prompt shapes, and reduce per-request CPU cycles used by tokenization by >=40% for cached/hot paths.

Scope: Engineering work involves runtime prefill pipeline changes (C++/Rust layer), in-process LRU cache, optional shared Redis cache for cross-worker reuse, and integration with request batching so identical prompts within a batch re-use tokenized outputs. We will also add instrumentation and dashboards for tracking hits/misses and CPU savings.

High-level approach and constraints:
- Fast-path tokenizer for ASCII/UTF-8 simple prompts: skip expensive unicode normalization if heuristics pass (ASCII-only, length < 2048 chars, no control chars, not JSON or CSV typed input). Use byte-level BPE lookup and preallocated buffers to avoid per-request allocations.
- Use HuggingFace tokenizers (Rust) via our existing FFI bridge; replace per-request allocations with reuse of a thread-local Tokenizer instance and pre-reserved Vecs for ids/attention masks.
- Multi-tier caching: (1) in-process LRU keyed by normalized prompt+model+template+version (small TTL, default 1h), (2) optional shared Redis pretokenized store for Dedicated/Private deployments where cross-worker reuse matters. Keys are sha256(normalized_prompt||model||runtime_version||template_hash).
- Ensure cache invalidation when system prompts, templates, or tokenizer version changes. Include schema version in cache key.
- Batch-level dedupe: when a prefill batch contains identical prompt texts, reuse the single tokenization result across requests instead of re-tokenizing N times.
- Measurement: add metrics tokenization_duration_ms, tokenization_cpu_ns, tokenized_cache_hits, tokenized_cache_misses, tokenization_alloc_bytes. Add per-route breakdown in Console and a dedicated perf dashboard.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Cache hits improve latency but can leak PII if not careful; we will only cache raw token ID arrays, never store original text in shared caches, and for Private deployments add KMS tagging to control shared cache permissions. For PII-sensitive customers we will respect a 'no_cache' header and disable shared caching.
- Fast-path heuristics might misclassify inputs (e.g., non-ASCII characters invisible to heuristics). We'll fall back to full tokenizer on any suspicious cases. Extensive unit tests and fuzzing will be used.
- Redis shared cache introduces network hops; it's optional and behind a deployment flag. For hosted API we'll prefer in-process cache + batch dedupe.

Acceptance criteria (see acceptance_criteria field): performance targets met in benchmark, automated tests present, feature flag + canary rollout plan, dashboard to monitor impact.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarked p50 tokenization latency <4ms and p95 <10ms on representative small/medium prompts using hosted-worker profile
Instrumented metrics: tokenization_duration_ms, tokenized_cache_hits, tokenized_cache_misses visible in Console dashboard
In-process LRU cache enabled behind feature flag; shared Redis cache optional via config; both honor 'no_cache' request flag
Batch-level dedupe implemented in prefill scheduler and validated with unit + integration tests
Rollout plan with canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and automated rollback if tokenization_error_rate > 0.1% or p99 request latency regresses by >5%
PRs merged with code review and CI green; conformance tests for tokenizer version skew and cache invalidation
perf_benchmarks: Baseline (2026-02): p50=11.2ms, p95=21.7ms for tokenization+normalization on m5-large hosted nodes at N=1
Target: p50<4ms, p95<10ms for common prompts; CPU cycles reduction >=40% for cached/hot-paths
Microbench: ascii-only fast-path tokenization: ~0.9ms median on warm thread-local Tokenizer with preallocated buffers
Shared cache hit scenario: end-to-end prefill latency improvement 20-45% depending on prompt reuse

notes: Implementation language: prefer Rust tokenizers via existing FFI for consistency with other runtime components
Cache key includes tokenizer_schema_v2 to force invalidation on tokenizer algorithm changes
For Dedicated/Private clusters where Redis is enabled, add configuration toggle and RBAC for shared cache access
